record.paper: On a conjecture by Anthony Hill

dossier_meta.paper: On a conjecture by Anthony Hill
dossier_meta.statement_text: The crossing number of $M_{n,t}$ is equal to $$H(n) - \frac{1}{2}\,t(k-1)(k-2),$$ where $k = \lfloor n/2 \rfloor$.
dossier_meta.context_text: Here $M_{n,t}$ denotes the graph obtained from $K_n$ by removing a matching of size $t$, and $k = \lfloor n/2 \rfloor$. Corollary 4 shows that geodesic drawings of $M_{n,t}$ built from sets of strength $0$ achieve this crossing count; the existence of many such sets of strength $0$ motivates the conjecture that this value is optimal.
